---
title: "Wave-1 cutover packets: Calendar, Mail, Apps, Finance, Meet, Roadmap"
description: "Per-app Worker identity, routes, bindings, build commands, rollback and smoke checks for the wave-1 Cloudflare cutover."
updatedAt: "2026-11-17"
audience: developers
---

Each packet covers an app's cutover to its native Cloudflare Worker and recovery
after activation. Provider writes (DNS, routes,
custom domains, aliases, deployments) stay with the release operator; the source
only produces the sealed Worker bytes. Secret values never appear here, only names.

## Common

- Build (CI parity): `bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/<app> --concurrency=2`, then
  `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-artifact.mjs prepare <app> production <sha> <workers-subdomain>`,
  `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-runtime.mjs <app> production <sha>` (needs `CI=true`) and
  `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-publish.mjs dry-run <app> production <sha>`.
- Finance's package `build` is its Vercel Next build, so its producer build is
  `bun turbo:local run build --filter="@tuturuuu/finance^..." --concurrency=2`, then
  `VITE_FINANCE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production bun run build:cloudflare` in `apps/finance`, then
  `VITE_FINANCE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production python3 scripts/ci/finance-native-artifact.py config apps/finance`
  before the shared prepare step. Its publication config keeps the emitted vars exactly.
- Calendar, Mail, Apps and Finance release recipe records use a closed schema inside
  `scripts/ci/wave1-native-profiles.json`. Each declares public origins, allowed vars,
  secret names, committed build recipe, compatibility settings and bounded smoke
  expectations. The sealed policy digest covers the record. Reseal sealed unpublished
  artifacts after policy edits, even when the emitted publication config is identical.
- The production publication profile (`scripts/ci/wave1-native-profiles.json`) uploads a
  route-free Worker (`workers_dev: false`, `routes: []`). Binding the canonical host is a
  separate provider step, so uploading never moves traffic.
- Finance production-only records publish the qualified emitted vars exactly.
  Legacy secret lists and identities are cross-checked against recipe records.
  Staging URLs must resolve to staging hosts; smoke paths remain on the fixed
  admitted origin.
- Executor errors inherit provider-contact state. Only explicit, proven pre-contact
  policy/validation/admission refusals may report no contact; upload and verification
  uncertainty requires reconciliation. Lease renewals extend the lease budget while
  retaining the fixed maximum job duration.
- The `cf-wave1` queue adapter is offline and accepts only an injected deploy
  authority. Missing authority prevents execution. It provides explicit seal,
  publish, doctor and rollback phase identities; rollback requires an authorized
  recorded deployment and matching readback. It does not attach routes, promote,
  install a scheduler or activate provider execution.
- Production publication is gated by `productionPublicationPolicy` in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`
  and the `wave1-native-production.yaml` dispatch, which lists `calendar`, `mail`, `apps`
  and `finance`. All four are admitted. Each run uses the protected GitHub environment
  `wave1-<app>-production` (`publish` only succeeds when `PUBLICATION_ENVIRONMENT` equals that
  exact name) and must be dispatched from the `production` ref.
- Environments the release owner creates (restrict each to the `production` branch and add a
  required reviewer): `wave1-calendar-production`,
  `wave1-mail-production`, `wave1-apps-production`, `wave1-finance-production`. Each holds the same four secrets,
  by name: `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_URL`, `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (public build
  inputs), `WAVE1_PRODUCTION_CLOUDFLARE_READ_TOKEN` (read-only topology, used by the
  preflight and verify steps) and `WAVE1_PRODUCTION_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (upload only, used
  by the upload step). The per-app Worker secrets listed below are set on the Worker, not
  in GitHub.
- The production planner contains no Vercel publishers.
- Tasks and Track are not wave-1 profile apps. Their `mail-calendar-tasks-builds.yaml`
  (`tasks-cutover-artifact`) and `track-cloudflare.yaml` (`track-cutover-artifact`) jobs
  already rewrite the emitted config to the production Worker names `tuturuuu-tasks` and
  `tuturuuu-track` (route-free, `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off) and upload the
  artifact for an operator cf publication ([D74 runbook](/build/devops/d74-cutover-runbooks),
  step 4). Tasks now has a production publisher (`tasks-cloudflare.yaml`); Track
  has none and needs no environment.
- For Calendar, Mail and Apps, record the currently assigned Worker version and
  its production smoke results before assigning a candidate. Restore a previously
  verified Cloudflare version with `assign --worker <worker> --version <previous>
  --expect-current <regressing>` while keeping the active routes in place. If the
  version check fails, capture the live deployment again and reconcile ownership.
  If the app has no previously verified Cloudflare version, publish a targeted fix.
- Smoke, after the flip, per host `<host>`:

  ```sh
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<host>/            # expect 200 or the login redirect 307, never 5xx
  curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://<host>/login | head -1             # expect 200 or 307 to tuturuuu.com/login
  curl -sS https://<host>/api/build-info                                # expect the exact source sha and runtime native
  ```

  A passing smoke shows `server: cloudflare` and no `x-vercel-id` header.

## Verified at `506c1ea9`

The full production-profile sequence (build, seal, original-bytes workerd acceptance,
upload-limit dry-run, final seal) passes on an isolated checkout for these apps:

| App | Script bytes | Gzip bytes | Modules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Calendar | 23181018 | 3315032 | 221 |
| Mail | 6123439 | 1958325 | 103 |
| Apps | 2355083 | 567748 | 25 |

Every size is inside the recorded paid-plan limits (64 MiB script). Mail and Apps runtime
acceptance returns `200` for `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info`, `405` for `POST`, and `307` for the
unauthenticated workspace route. Meet and Roadmap use their own workflows and are covered above.

## Calendar

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-calendar` |
| Canonical host | `calendar.tuturuuu.com` |
| Secrets (names) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID`, `CRON_SECRET`; optional `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` |
| Bindings | `ASSETS` only; no database, KV, R2 or queue |
| Publication | Admitted in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`; dispatch `wave1-native-production.yaml` with `app=calendar` from `production` (environment `wave1-calendar-production`) |
| Rollback | Previous `tuturuuu-calendar` version verified on the canonical host |

The production artifact uses `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_CALENDAR=shadow` to serve both
`calendar.tuturuuu.com` and `tuturuuu.com/calendar` before traffic activation.
After verifying the mounted artifact and login handoff, set the mode to `on`
to enable the subdomain redirect and service-worker cleanup. The existing
Google and Microsoft starts and callbacks continue to run on
`calendar.tuturuuu.com`. Moving the callbacks to the apex requires registering
and verifying both new redirect URIs with their providers. Artifact acceptance
checks asset bytes on both hosts and the legacy completion document on the
subdomain.

## Mail

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-mail` |
| Canonical host | `mail.tuturuuu.com` |
| Secrets (names) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, `MAIL_CONNECTED_ACCOUNTS_KEY`, `MAIL_R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `MAIL_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `MAIL_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MAIL_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `MAIL_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `MAIL_CLOUDFLARE_INGEST_SECRET` |
| Resources | Existing R2 bucket `tuturuuu-mail` (retained); the email-routing Worker (`wrangler.email-routing.jsonc`) is a separate deployment and is not touched by this cutover |
| Publication | Admitted in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`; dispatch `wave1-native-production.yaml` with `app=mail` from `production` (environment `wave1-mail-production`) |
| Rollback | Previous `tuturuuu-mail` version verified on the canonical host |

Qualify each inbound webhook before moving its route to the Mail Worker.
Verify the sender's actual request path and authentication, and verify delivery
through the new path. Check the other webhook and leave mail delivery DNS records
in place while changing one route.

## Apps

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-apps` |
| Canonical host | `apps.tuturuuu.com`; the production profile sets `APPS_CANONICAL_HOST_ENABLED=1`, without which the Worker answers 503 on that host |
| Admitted apex mount | `https://tuturuuu.com/apps` |
| Secrets (names) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` |
| Vars | `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN=https://tuturuuu.com`; `/api/*` proxies to Web |
| Publication | Admitted in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`; dispatch `wave1-native-production.yaml` with `app=apps` from `production` (environment `wave1-apps-production`) |
| Rollback | Previous verified `tuturuuu-apps` version. Revert a gateway-only regression on the gateway. |

The sealed production profile is checked on the canonical host and at
`/apps` on the apex. Original and archive-restored checks verify the rendered
launcher links, repeated and encoded query parameters through redirects,
mounted CSS and JavaScript bytes, and 404s outside the mount. Routing is
configured separately by the release operator.

## Finance

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-finance` (production only; `finance-cloudflare.yaml` qualifies staging) |
| Canonical host | `finance.tuturuuu.com` |
| Admitted apex mount | `https://tuturuuu.com/finance`; the production Worker rejects other apex paths and hosts |
| Secrets (names) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`; the Worker refuses to start without the last two |
| Vars | The production entry of `apps/finance/cloudflare/native-profiles.json`: `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `FINANCE_APP_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. The Supabase URL is a var, so it is not a Worker secret |
| Compatibility | `2026-10-12`, `nodejs_compat` and `global_fetch_strictly_public`, from `apps/finance/void.config.ts` |
| Publication | Admitted in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`; dispatch `wave1-native-production.yaml` with `app=finance` from `production` (environment `wave1-finance-production`) |
| Anonymous `/` | 307 to `https://tuturuuu.com/login`; the pre-seal doctor runs with `--expect-redirect` |

Production Workerd acceptance checks the build identity on both hosts,
including `/finance/api/build-info` on the apex, before and after restoring the
sealed archive. The staging profile serves only its own root host.

## Meet

`meet.tuturuuu.com` is already served by the `tuturuuu-meet` Worker (`server: cloudflare`,
anonymous `/` answers 307 to the Web login). Source carries the custom-domain route in
`apps/meet/void.config.ts`. Bindings: `ASSETS`, `WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE`, `ABUSE_GUARD`
(service `tuturuuu-abuse-guard`), R2 cache bucket `tuturuuu-meet-cache`,
`IMAGES`, and the `MEET_LIVE` Durable Object (migration tag `meet-live-v1`). Required secret
names: `MEET_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`.
Meet is not part of the wave-1 profile set: `meet-cloudflare.yaml` validates it on every
change (native build, emitted-config receipt, restored-artifact acceptance) and its `deploy`
job publishes from the `production` ref with a deployment marker. Meet AI stays contained (`MEET_AI_DISABLED=true`). Migration changes follow the Meet
migration serialization and are not part of this packet. Vercel holds no READY production
deployment for Meet (all recent ones are canceled), so rollback for a Meet regression is the
previous Worker version, not Vercel.

## Roadmap

The `tuturuuu-roadmap` Worker serves `tuturuuu.com/roadmap*`. Cloudflare routes
match the full URL, so the terminal wildcard covers query strings on the bare
mount. The Worker passes sibling paths such as `/roadmapping` to the zone origin.
Web's fallback proxy fetches the apex route and guards against recursion.

- Publication: verify the emitted route in the sealed artifact. The provider
  owner attaches or verifies `tuturuuu.com/roadmap*` during deployment. A Worker
  version promotion alone does not update zone routes.
- Rollback: restore the captured Worker version and zone route set together.
- Smoke: run `node apps/roadmap/scripts/canonical-smoke.mjs` after publication.
  The canonical English and Vietnamese pages must return HTML with HTTP 200 for
  both ordinary queries and UTM parameters.
